topic_control.interpretation: Llama > Med42 in both baselines; finding is robust to baseline choice.

causal_ablation.interpretation: In Llama, shared-dim ablation causes specific extra drop beyond random in both categories (+12pts CH, +6pts MI), indicating causal role. In Med42, same dim ablation has no specific effect over random (-12pts CH, 0pts MI), indicating the shared circuit has been redistributed and those specific dimensions no longer carry the safety signal. Direct causal support for the fragmentation hypothesis.

med42_native_ablation.interpretation: Med42-native shared dims at layer 25 are not specifically causal for refusal; differential is non-positive in both categories. Combined with the Llama-native ablation (also non-causal in Med42), this supports fragmentation rather than relocation: the shared substrate does not exist as a localized causal unit at any analogous layer in Med42 we probed.

paper_interpretation: Medical fine-tuning fragments the shared information-integrity refusal subspace rather than relocating it. Evidence: (1) reduced cross-category Jaccard overlap, (2) loss of specific causal role for base-Llama shared coordinates in Med42, and (3) Med42-native ablation also fails to find a localized causal substrate.

llama_multiseed_ablation.interpretation: Multi-seed (n=10) random-control sweep at base Llama layer 22 confirms the focal-pair shared-dim ablation effect is statistically distinguishable from random null for community-health (z=+2.45, ~99th percentile) but not for misinformation (z=-0.50, null). The focal pair's shared dimensions therefore have a verified causal role on one of the two regressed behaviors in base Llama. The misinformation regression mechanism remains unclear at the layer/coordinates we tested.
